_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.english_concept: block / print letters vs. cursive, as school scripts
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, tool selector labels, title qualifier
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the script selector on an it handwriting-sheet generator, and offer the maiuscolo/minuscolo split rather than a single 'block letters' option — that split is the locally expected granularity. 'Corsivo' is the counterpart for the joined script.
phrases.good_example: Scegli il carattere: stampatello maiuscolo, stampatello minuscolo o corsivo.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'corsivo' on this site without context: in Italian typography 'corsivo' also means italic type, exactly the ambiguity the existing IT-024 record touches. On a handwriting page, anchor it with 'corsivo (lettere legate)' or with the stampatello contrast so the school sense is unambiguous.

phrases.register: neutral, teacher-facing, also used by parents
phrases.content_surface: h1, title, meta_description, faq
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the it head term for the alphabet-chart job: 'alfabetiere murale da stampare'. 'Murale' (wall) vs 'da banco' (desk) is the standard size distinction Italian sites offer — a genuine, locally expected product variant, not decoration.
phrases.good_example: Alfabetiere murale da stampare — una lettera per foglio A4.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for a single-letter page or a colouring sheet — an alfabetiere is by definition the whole A–Z set as a display object. Do not translate it as 'abecedario'-style; there is no Italian equivalent of that Spanish kids/technical split.

phrases.english_concept: a lettering tattoo (the tattooed text itself) — consumer word vs studio word
phrases.content_surface: h2_h3, intro_copy, faq, internal_link_anchor
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'scritta' for the thing the user is making ('la tua scritta al polso') and 'lettering' when naming the style family or the discipline. Keep 'font per tatuaggio' (IT-018) as the head/query term.
phrases.good_example: Il polso interno è la zona iconica per scritte brevi: parole singole, nomi, con un font minimalista o uno script corsivo.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'scritta' to mean 'font' — it names the text, never the typeface. Do not use borrowed 'lettering' in a plain consumer FAQ answer where 'scritta' is clearer; and note this borrowing is Italian/Spanish-specific — do not propagate it into the French page (see P11).

phrases.english_concept: text-built face emoticon — the everyday Italian word
phrases.content_surface: h1, category headings, tool copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Good as the friendly head noun ('Faccine da copiare e incollare'). Pair with 'emoticon giapponesi' or 'kaomoji' when the page is specifically about upright Japanese faces.
phrases.good_example: Faccine da copiare e incollare: oltre 500 emoticon fatte solo con caratteri.
phrases.avoid_when: Too soft for tryhard/competitive gaming nickname copy (IT-027 'nomi tryhard / sweaty' register applies there). Not for technical Unicode explanations.

phrases.native_phrase: si leggono orizzontalmente, senza dover inclinare la testa
phrases.english_concept: the sideways-vs-upright distinction, in the natively Italian phrasing
phrases.content_surface: faq, first-paragraph explainer, section intro
phrases.usage_guidance: Use this exact framing in the Italian explainer sentence rather than translating the English 'read upright'. Contrast with 'i nostri classici smile' for the Western sideways form — the possessive 'i nostri' is a natively Italian touch that a translation engine will not produce.
phrases.good_example: A differenza dei nostri classici smile, i kaomoji si leggono orizzontalmente, senza dover inclinare la testa.
phrases.avoid_when: Body/FAQ copy only — it's a sentence, not a search term. Never in a title or meta.

phrases.register: neutral; the standard, non-optional industry and consumer term
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq, body copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use whenever the Italian copy refers to a wedding invitation, in place of any 'invito' phrasing. It supports an existing script/corsivo page's target (IT-024 corsivo elegante); it is not itself a page to build.
phrases.good_example: Per le partecipazioni si sceglie di solito un font calligrafico per i nomi degli sposi e uno neutro per data e indirizzo.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Note it means the printed announcement card specifically — for a party invite or a save-the-date, Italians do say 'invito'/'Save the Date', so do not over-apply it.

phrases.english_concept: the script/calligraphic font family, in its Italian trade name
phrases.content_surface: body copy, faq, style-description text
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to name the look on a formal-occasion section; keep 'corsivo' (IT-024) as the page's primary term since that is what Italians type when they want a copy-paste style. 'Font calligrafico' is a supporting synonym, not a replacement target.
phrases.good_example: Un font calligrafico funziona per i nomi; per il resto del testo serve qualcosa di più silenzioso.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Avoid using the trade nicknames ('i graziati', 'i bastoni') outside a genuinely typographic explanation — in general copy they read as showing off.

phrases.native_phrase: deve essere leggibile anche dalla zia anziana
phrases.english_concept: the legibility test people actually apply to a decorative script
phrases.content_surface: faq heading or body copy — not h1/title
phrases.usage_guidance: Excellent framing for an FAQ answer about when an ornate script is too much. It works as a memorable native phrasing of a universal caution; it does not target a query and must not displace the page's primary term.
phrases.good_example: Regola pratica: le partecipazioni devono essere lette anche dalla zia anziana.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages — the site already has IT-020 (uso eccessivo) for over-decoration criticism in the gaming register, and mixing the two registers on one page is the failure mode to avoid. Also avoid on accessibility copy: this is a folksy heuristic, not an accessibility standard, and must not be used as a substitute for one.

phrases.english_concept: bold text in a LinkedIn post, and the professional-risk framing
phrases.content_surface: h1/h2 for an Italian LinkedIn-bold page, faq, body copy
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the literal Italian query. Pair the how-to with the native caution ('se evidenzi tutto, non evidenzi niente') — Italian sources are consistent that the *headline* specifically should be left unstyled, which is a usable, locally-evidenced piece of guidance.
phrases.good_example: Troppa formattazione rende il post artificioso e fa perdere credibilità.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not carry the gaming register (IT-015 'nick dark / tryhard', IT-027 'nomi tryhard') anywhere near this. Do not present styled bold as recommended for the profile title — Italian sources explicitly advise against it there.

phrases.native_phrase: il risultato cambia da app a app
phrases.english_concept: platform-dependent rendering — the same pasted styled text behaves differently in each app
phrases.register: neutral, first-person troubleshooting voice; used by ordinary users, not documentation
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, troubleshooting h2, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the IT FAQ heading for the compatibility question («Perché il risultato cambia da app a app?») and answer it by naming the apps the user actually named — Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, TikTok — rather than abstracting to 'some platforms'. Enumerating named surfaces is what makes the Italian answer read as written by someone who has tested it. Supports, never replaces, the page's primary target (IT-001 caratteri speciali / IT-013 font copia e incolla).
phrases.good_example: Il risultato cambia da app a app: su Instagram di solito funziona, su Facebook desktop alcuni caratteri spariscono.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a title/H1 term — it is a symptom sentence. Do not use it when the real cause is a character limit (IT-016) or a rejected name; the answer would be wrong. Do not soften it into a device-vs-device claim ('dipende dal telefono'), which is a different and usually incorrect diagnosis.

phrases.native_phrase: i caratteri spariscono / scompaiono del tutto
phrases.english_concept: characters vanish entirely on paste — a third failure mode, distinct from boxes and from garbling
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, body, tool warning copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep it as its own FAQ item alongside quadratini (IT-010) — do not merge them into one 'i caratteri non funzionano' answer, because the fixes differ: a box means the viewer's font lacks the glyph (choose a different style), a disappearance means the destination field filtered it out (the style is unusable there at all). Pair it with P1: the disappearance is app-specific, which is why the user sees it in one app only.
phrases.good_example: Su alcune app i caratteri non diventano quadratini: spariscono del tutto, quindi il nome salvato risulta più corto di quello che hai incollato.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a title/H1 term. Do not use it for the box/tofu case (IT-010) or for the mojibake case (P3) — Italian users read the three as different problems, and conflating them makes the answer visibly wrong. Avoid in marketing/reassurance copy near the copy button, where it seeds doubt without offering the fix.

phrases.native_phrase: caratteri strani al posto delle lettere accentate / simboli strani al posto degli accenti
phrases.english_concept: mojibake — garbled characters shown where accented letters should be (Italian has no native single word for it)
phrases.register: neutral, non-technical; identical wording from 2008 forum posts to 2020 Microsoft Q&A, i.e. a stable, durable formulation
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, troubleshooting h2, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the IT FAQ heading for the garbled-paste question, and put the visible symptom in the heading or first line — Italians recognise «Ã¨» on sight and it confirms in one glance that the page is about their problem. Keep it separate from quadratini (IT-010): a box is a missing glyph, this is misread bytes. Do NOT use it for the decorative-Unicode failure — Italian mojibake is overwhelmingly an accented-letter problem, so this FAQ answers a text-handling question, not a styling one.
phrases.good_example: Se vedi caratteri strani al posto delle lettere accentate (per esempio «Ã¨» invece di «è») il problema è la codifica del testo, non il generatore.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a title/H1 term. Do not use it for boxes (IT-010) or for characters that vanish (P2). Do not use the technical framing «problema di codifica» as the heading — that is the cause, and users search the symptom.

phrases.native_phrase: l'apostrofo al posto delle lettere accentate (perche', citta', cosi', e')
phrases.english_concept: the Italian workaround for accented vowels that cannot survive a transform — write the apostrophe instead of the accent (perche', citta', e')
phrases.register: neutral; historically standard on Italian internet, though today it reads slightly dated/informal in polished prose — fine for nicknames, bios and captions, which is our use case
phrases.content_surface: faq answer, body, tool copy — not h1, not the heading itself
phrases.usage_guidance: Offer it as the practical fix in the answer to the accented-letters FAQ, exactly as a German page offers ae/oe/ue. Say why it works: the apostrophe form is a real Italian convention, not a spelling mistake. Then state the one thing the user actually needs to know — that dropping the accent altogether is NOT equivalent, because «è» (verb 'to be') and «e» (conjunction 'and') are different words, so a styled caption that silently loses the accent changes what the sentence says. That sentence is the whole reason this record exists.
phrases.good_example: Nessun alfabeto Unicode decorativo contiene à, è, é, ì, ò, ù: se ti serve la parola intera nello stesso stile, usa l'apostrofo al posto dell'accento (perche', citta', e'). Non togliere e basta l'accento: «è» e «e» sono due parole diverse.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not recommend it in formal, legal, accessibility or educational copy, or on printable/handwriting-practice pages, where correct orthography is the point — there the right advice is to keep é and accept that it stays unstyled. Do not present it as 'correct Italian spelling'; it is a compatibility convention. Not a title/H1 term.

phrases.english_concept: the line-break action that produces stacked text in a bio/caption
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq heading, tool copy, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use «andare a capo» as the heading/action name and «Invio» as the key name in any instruction. Mention the iPhone case explicitly — an Italian instruction that just says 'premi Invio' will fail for a large share of the audience, and saying so is what makes the page look tested rather than translated.
phrases.good_example: Per andare a capo nella bio premi Invio; su iPhone il tasto Invio non compare, quindi scrivi il testo nelle Note e incollalo.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it for a one-letter-per-line decorative effect or for CJK-style vertical text — «andare a capo» is strictly the line-break action. Do not write «premi Enter»: the Italian key name is Invio.

phrases.english_concept: the platform silently removing the blank lines / spacing the user added
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in the FAQ answer about why the spacing vanished, and name which of the two failed: «l'a capo resta, gli spazi vuoti no». Then offer the invisible-character fix (IT-009 / IT-023 — the Braille blank is already the community-known codepoint in this locale, so it is the natural thing to point at).
phrases.good_example: Se lasci righe bianche nella bio, l'applicazione le rimuove in automatico appena salvi.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a title/H1 term. Do not use it for the Unicode-glyph failures (IT-010 quadratini, P2 spariscono) — this is formatting being stripped, not characters being unsupported, and the fixes are unrelated.

phrases.content_surface: counter-page copy, FAQ
phrases.usage_guidance: Label the IT counter's char stat 'battute (spazi inclusi)' — it is the term limits are issued in; the fetched thread's author didn't know how to count them in Word.

phrases.content_surface: title, h1, faq
phrases.usage_guidance: Direct forum-verified demand for the scored 'wedding monogram/initials cursive-lettering generator' opportunity — users currently default to Canva/DaFont/PowerPoint, no purpose-built tool found.

phrases.content_surface: title/H1/meta, faq
phrases.usage_guidance: Fits an Italian wedding-lettering or elegant-script usecase page (mirrors FR-043 faire-part de mariage). No existing IT page uses this term yet — genuinely new coverage, not a rewording of an existing page.
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — mainstream, formal/aspirational register

phrases.content_surface: title|meta
phrases.usage_guidance: Italian uses "da copiare": simboli da copiare 720/mo, cuori da copiare 260/mo. The IT head term itself is caratteri speciali (40,500/mo), with simboli as the browse-register synonym.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not lead a title with "da copiare"; it qualifies the head noun.
